short: ASR transcripts as training labels (M02) are standard (Afouras 2020, Ma 2022); scale cuts LRS3 VSR WER to 19.1%, but no run spread is reported and USR 2.0 reaches 17.6%.
position: Auto-AVSR [@ma2023autoavsr] changes one component, the training labels (M02), adding 2,630 h of video transcribed by a public ASR model. The design is standard: Afouras et al. trained lip readers with CTC on ASR-generated transcripts of unlabelled video [@afouras2020asr], and the same group had already added AVSpeech with automatically generated transcriptions [@ma2022multilingual]; the paper adds scale (641 h to 2,630 h) and four labellers. With the model fixed, LRS3 visual-only WER falls from 33.0% to 19.1% as automatic-label hours grow (Table 2), but the [later] USR 2.0 reaches 17.6% on the same two corpora with self-generated labels and no language model [@haliassos2026usr2]. Evaluation (M12) reports no run count, seeds or spread, unlike the ten-run means of the group's prior work [@ma2022multilingual], so the labeller ranking (Table 1) is not established; the 30% headline names no baseline.
